title: A connector's label can sit in a break in its line
body:
Today a connector's `label` sits beside its line, on the side `label-side` picks, at `label-at`. `sweep` takes no label. The sufr pipeline figure in `sufr-figures` names each step on its arrow by stopping the line, setting the word on the line's path, and starting a second arrow below the word. That is three nodes per arrow, with the gap worked out by hand.

## Proposal

- `label-side on` sets the label centred on the line at `label-at`, and leaves a gap in the line around the label's box.
- `sweep` takes `label`, `label-at` and `label-side` as `arrow` does.

```text
arrow { from ranks bottom; to key top; label "prefix encoder scheme"; label-side on; }
```

## Open

- Whether the gap around the label is fixed or set by a property.
close_reason: Landed in 859da28. `LabelSide::On` centers the label on the path, and `Connector::draw` cuts the path where it lies inside the label's box padded by `LABEL_GAP` (`leave_box`). A sweep splits its cubic at the crossings (`cubic_gap`, `split`). `sweep` reads the label properties in `build::sweep`.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/0c799e42
notes.text: Jack accepted on 2026-11-23, provisionally: the break in the line is the label's padding, with no new property.
